narrative.northStar: The Notebook on a Calm Desk
narrative.overview:
Investing feels calmer when your reasons are written down. Portle looks like a tidy desk at night: a neutral charcoal surface, a few cards of your own lying on it at small angles (a portfolio, a note saying why you bought something, a comment from a friend), and one soft violet lamp of colour. It is friendly before it is clever. A first-time investor should feel welcome and unhurried; nothing on the page should look like a trading terminal.

The system has two rooms that share one palette of violet light, taken from the Portle symbol. The public landing page is the friendly front room: charcoal, roomy, rounded, with the product's own cards shown as tilted notes and a hand-drawn desk illustration to close. The signed-in app is the workroom: an ink-and-indigo glass shell with denser panels, tabular numerals and familiar controls. Both keep the Portle symbol, the violet action, the private-by-default promise and Gabarito for display type.
keyCharacteristics: Charcoal ground on the landing page; ink and indigo glass in the app. Violet is the only accent in both; the symbol's sky, cyan and ember appear only in data and in the mark itself.
Show the product, not a picture of it: the hero is made of real card components with sample data, labelled "Sample" or "Example".
Friendly geometry: pill actions, 18–28px cards, tilts of at most about five degrees.
Plain, warm copy that answers beginners' worries (passwords, privacy, cost, advice).
Numbers are tabular, and money is shown only to its owner; shared views use percentages.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Violet is the only accent. A screen lights one thing (the primary action, the step number, the selected row) and leaves the rest of the desk in charcoal.

rules.name: The Neutral Ground Rule
rules.body: The landing ground is a true neutral charcoal, not purple-black and not pure black. Warmth comes from the violet and the copy, not from tinting the ground.

rules.name: The Friendly Bold Rule
rules.body: Headlines are bold and rounded, never thin or condensed; emphasis comes from size and weight, never from gradient text.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can be compared (weights, returns, balances, dates in a rail) is set with tabular, lining figures.

rules.name: The Paper-On-A-Desk Rule
rules.body: Landing cards are opaque paper, not glass: a soft offset shadow, a light edge, and a tilt of at most about five degrees. Glass belongs to the app.

rules.name: The One Drawing Rule
rules.body: The hand-drawn violet illustration appears once, to close the page (its plate was drawn in lilac and is turned 13° toward violet in CSS). Everything else shows the real product.

dos: Do show real product components with sample data in the hero, and label them "Sample" or "Example".
Do keep one violet accent lit per screen and leave the rest in charcoal and soft text.
Do answer beginners' worries in plain words (no broker passwords, only you see your numbers, free to start, not investment advice).
Do set every comparable number with tabular figures, and show money values only to their owner. Shared views use percentages.
Do put white labels only on indigo-violet (action-indigo or deeper); lighter violets and lavenders carry ink text.
Do draw icons from one stroke family (lucide at 1.4–1.8) or as small inline SVG.
donts: Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading; the heading carries itself.
Don't use glass, neon glows or dramatic spotlights on the landing page; it is paper on a desk.
Don't use gradient text, coloured side stripes, or Unicode glyphs and emoji as icons.
Don't tilt anything more than about five degrees, or tilt text that people need to read at length.
Don't use semantic green or red outside data (returns, gains, losses, import results).
Don't reproduce third-party logos in sample data; use letter tiles.
